thread:
sam: Quick question — when we create presigned export links from the console, how do we ensure the download is still auditable and revocable if a user's role changes after the link is issued?

maya: Good callout. Right now presigned URLs are purely time-limited S3 objects, no link back to the current RBAC state. Means if someone loses permission we can't revoke unless we rotate the object.

arnav: Two quick ideas: include an "export_epoch" token in the manifest that maps to auth state at issuance, and require a short-lived streaming endpoint that validates the epoch on each chunk. That lets us revoke by bumping epoch.

kelsie: I like epoch linking. UX question: console should show "Export will be invalidated if your role changes" and a clear timestamp. Also, we need telemetry events for who clicked download, not just who triggered the export job.

sam: epoch token sounds neat — what would the API shape look like?

arnav: Proposal: export manifest includes {"export_id":"...","epoch_id":"E2026-03-21-42"}. Download endpoint /v1/exports/:id/stream requires header X-Export-Epoch: E..., and we validate epoch == current_allowed_epoch_for(actor). If mismatch -> 403.

maya: Implementation detail: store epoch mapping in a small fast kv (redis) with TTL. When a role change or entitlement revocation happens, bump epoch for that tenant/actor and expire old ones. We already have code paths that touch redis for rate limits so we can reuse.

kelsie: For presigned S3 downloads we can still keep them but make them short (5m) and have console request a streaming token that exchanges to a very short presigned URL per-chunk. That keeps S3 visible for compliance while giving us runtime revocation.

sam: What about audit logs? We need both: (1) event that export job was created, (2) event that export manifest was generated, (3) event that download was initiated (and ideally chunk-level resume events).

export-bot: log: EXPORT_CREATED tenant=acme user=sam export_id=exp_01 epoch=E2026-03-21-42

arnav: Agree. Minimal required fields in audit event: actor, tenant_id, export_id, epoch_id, ip, user_agent, action=(create|manifest_gen|download_start|download_chunk|download_complete). Keep shape compact for NDJSON exports.

maya: For downstream exports (customers consuming via webhook/stream) we should attach a signed proof header: X-Export-Proof: signed(tenant,export_id,epoch,ts). Helps external processors verify provenance.

kelsie: Console rollout UX: add a toggle "Enable revocable streaming" that defaults on for enterprise tenants. Show a small modal when you create an export explaining revocation policy. Also we need to surface "why download was blocked" in the UI when 403 hits (role changed / epoch mismatch).

sam: One implementation concern: extra redis lookups for each chunk may increase latency and cost. Could we only validate at stream start and then validate every N chunks?

arnav: We can accept a tradeoff: validate at start + periodic (every 1MB or every 30s). That covers most revocations without per-chunk checks. Make it configurable per tenant.

maya: Ops ask: telemetry for download failures should include failure_reason (epoch_mismatch/expired_token/forbidden). That helps SREs debug false positives.

kelsie: Also include a console-level "Export activity" panel that shows recent downloads with actor, ip, result (success/fail), and a link to the raw NDJSON audit bundle for legal.

sam: OK agreed. Action items:
- arnav: draft API contract for manifest + X-Export-Epoch + proof header (PR by EOD Fri).
- maya: prototype redis epoch mapping and a short-lived streaming token service (spike next week).
- kelsie: design console copy + download-block modal + telemetry panel (mock by Thu).
- infra: limit default presigned URL TTL to 5m and add logic to mint per-chunk presigned URLs when streaming is enabled.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/exports-epoch-check -> staging (build 4231)

sam: Thanks all. We'll discuss API contract in eng-platform API review tomorrow.
